content.text: the youth is usually seen alone, sometimes with a parent (especially with special health care needs); HEEADSSS (home, education, eating, activities, drugs, sexuality, suicide, safety) or SSHADESS (strengths, school, home, activities, drugs, emotions/eating/depression, sexuality, safety) can organize the questions.

how they stay healthy; what they're good at; how they help others; important adults in their life; responsibilities at home and school; what they do with friends; health problems, concerns or questions.

questions about physical well-being, growth or puberty; something the child does well; concerns about emotional well-being, feelings, behavior or learning; what they've discussed about healthy lifestyle and avoiding risky behaviors; behaviors they're concerned about.
any specialty or emergency care since the last visit.
any new health condition or death in the family; if yes, who has or had it, age at onset and diagnosis, or age at death.

frequent headaches or dizziness; fainting; eyes or vision; ears or hearing; nose or throat; breathing problems or chest pain; belly pain, vomiting, bowel problems; painful urination or other urine problems; rashes, moles, sunburn; muscle aches, injury or other problems; fatigue. Girls: first period yet; last period; problems with periods; vaginal itching, burning or discharge.
